# Forge Dependencies

## Purpose

The `dependencies` directory preserves unresolved engineering dependencies
that require later Forge investigation.

A Dependency records an unresolved engineering tension. It does not answer its
own question, establish its own resolution, or become an established premise
merely because it has been recorded.

---

## Lifecycle

A Dependency remains open while its central engineering tension remains
unresolved.

When the dependency enters the Forge, the Forge investigates the unresolved
question and may produce a bounded finding. Anvil inspection may then test that
finding or the complete resulting artifact.

Anvil survival establishes inspection evidence. It does not, by itself, accept
a Discovery, create Procedural Authority, authorize a procedure, or perform a
lifecycle transition unless applicable governance separately establishes that
result.

Where a dependency is resolved through a Discovery, the applicable Discovery
lifecycle governs the standing and status of that Discovery.

A Dependency does not promote itself to a Discovery. The dependency record
preserves the unresolved relationship until later investigation and applicable
lifecycle action establish a changed state.

---

## Relationship to Discovery Records

A Discovery may preserve an unresolved dependency in `Open Dependencies`.

Recording an Open Dependency does not establish the answer to that dependency
or make it part of the finding's established dependency basis.

When a historically preserved Open Dependency is later resolved or materially
advanced, the later state may be recorded through the applicable Discovery
structure, including a conditional `Dependency Resolution Record` where that
structure applies.

The historical unresolved state remains part of the record. Later resolution
does not silently rewrite earlier knowledge, authority, evidence, or lifecycle
state.

---

## Dependency Direction

Dependencies point forward from established findings toward unresolved work.

A later resolution must be supported by the investigation, evidence, authority,
and lifecycle relationships applicable to that resolution. Chronology,
numbering, repository placement, or subject similarity does not by itself
establish that relationship.

---
